question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5x}\cdot 5=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/5$ | ${e}^{4}/5$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e/5}^{{e}^{4}/5}\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{e/5}^{{e}^{4}/5}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$
